title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reading.body:
This is a provenance failure rather than a reporting failure. The record carries a headline about an investigation into duplicate license plate numbers, and the text supplied with it is a set of weather alerts for Kansas and neighbouring areas. The two do not describe the same thing, so the item cannot support the claim its title makes.

The mismatch sits at the point where article text is captured and attached to a record. Catching it would have required a check that the retrieved text actually contains the subject named in the headline, before the item was catalogued or published. A comparison of that kind is mechanical and would have flagged the item immediately.

What is not established is anything about the plate issue itself. The supplied text gives no names, no numbers and no outcome, so whether duplicate plates caused dangerous situations for Kansas drivers is not shown here. Whether an automated process produced the mismatch, and whether the investigation exists elsewhere, are also not established.

summary:
The supplied article text does not include the investigation into duplicate license plate numbers. It only shows a headline about that topic, followed by weather alerts for Kansas and nearby areas. The alerts list flood watches and warnings for many counties, with rainfall amounts from 0.25 to 3 inches, possible pockets of 4 to 6 inches, and 1 to 5 inches already reported in some places. Up to 2 more inches of rain is possible.

The alerts tell people to watch later forecasts, prepare for possible flood warnings, and avoid driving on flooded roads. They cover central, south central, southwest, and west central Kansas, plus parts of Colorado and southwest Nebraska. The supplied text gives no details about who is involved in the plate issue, any key numbers for that story, or what happens next.
